#!/bin/sh
# Impeccable launcher. Runs the platform binary shipped next to this script:
#   <this dir>/bin/<os>-<arch>/impeccable
# Order: $IMPECCABLE_BIN, the sibling binary, ~/.impeccable/bin/impeccable,
# the version-pinned cache, then `impeccable` on PATH. Never needs Node.
# The unversioned home binary and the PATH candidate are validated with the
# engine-probe handshake first: the retired 3.x npm CLI also installed a bin
# named `impeccable`, and exec'ing it would fail every verb with
# "Unknown command". The sibling binary must also report the version in
# VERSION: it is gitignored, so a skill upgrade that copies files over this
# directory leaves the old engine in place. A local build of the same version
# passes, which is why it is not hashed. IMPECCABLE_BIN is the operator's
# explicit choice and is exec'd without a probe. The version-pinned cache and
# the download are verified against engine-checksums.txt (next to this
# script), never against anything published beside the binary; a
# <binary>.verified stamp holding the manifest digest and the binary's size
# skips rehashing until either changes or the binary is newer than the stamp.
# No path hashes on every run: hooks run this launcher on every edit.
set -eu

# True when the candidate answers the engine handshake (prints
# "impeccable-engine <version>", exit 0). Quiet and fast (<100ms).
# IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE marks the child as a probe: a copy of this
# launcher reached recursively (e.g. symlinked onto PATH as `impeccable`)
# then skips its own probes and refuses to download, so probing stays cheap
# and can never loop.
probe_ok() {
  probe_out=$(IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE=1 "$1" engine-probe 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  case "$probe_out" in
    impeccable-engine*) probe_version=${probe_out#impeccable-engine }; return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
probing=${IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE:-}
# Space, tab and CR, made once: hooks run this launcher on every edit and turn
# end, and every process it starts before the engine costs real time on a busy
# Windows machine (#1237), so the hot path below sticks to shell builtins.
ws=$(printf ' \t\r')

# Sets $digest_out to the digest engine-checksums.txt records for engine
# version $1 and asset $2 (lines are "<version> <asset> <sha256>"), empty when
# there is none.
# A CR is a separator too (CRLF checkouts), and a last line with no newline
# still counts.
manifest_digest() {
  digest_out=""
  [ -f "$manifest" ] || return 0
  while IFS="$ws" read -r m_version m_asset m_sum _ || [ -n "$m_version" ]; do
    case "$m_version" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
    if [ "$m_version" = "$1" ] && [ "$m_asset" = "$2" ]; then
      digest_out=$m_sum
      return 0
    fi
  done < "$manifest"
  return 0
}
# Sets $expected (and, on Windows on ARM, which runs x64 binaries,
# $expected_x64) from engine-checksums.txt.
read_expected() {
  manifest_digest "$version" "$asset"
  expected=$digest_out
  expected_x64=""
  if [ "$os" = windows ] && [ "$arch" = arm64 ]; then
    manifest_digest "$version" impeccable-windows-x64.exe
    expected_x64=$digest_out
  fi
}
# Sets $size to the byte count of the cached binary (BSD wc pads it).
cached_size() {
  size=$(wc -c < "$cached") || size=""
  size=${size##* }
}
# Sets $actual to the sha256 of $1, empty when no hash tool works.
hash_file() {
  actual=""
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if digest=$(shasum -a 256 "$1" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
  elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if digest=$(sha256sum "$1" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
  fi
}

# This script's directory without dirname or a subshell: what dirname "$0"
# gives, made absolute by a cd there and back.
case $0 in
  */*) dir=${0%/*} ;;
  *) dir=. ;;
esac
[ -n "$dir" ] || dir=/
caller_pwd=$PWD
CDPATH= cd -- "$dir" || { echo "impeccable: cannot enter the launcher directory $dir" >&2; exit 127; }
dir=$PWD
skill_dir=${dir%/*}
[ -n "$skill_dir" ] || skill_dir=/
cd -- "$caller_pwd" || { echo "impeccable: cannot return to $caller_pwd" >&2; exit 127; }
# VS Code syncs a plugin without the executable bit. Its hooks run this through
# sh, so restore the bit for the commands the skill runs directly (#1249).
[ -x "$0" ] || chmod +x "$0" 2>/dev/null || :
manifest="$dir/engine-checksums.txt"

# What the binary needs to know about its home: the skill directory (for
# reference/*.md and command-metadata.json) and how to name itself in the
# commands it prints. Exported BEFORE any exec below, including the
# IMPECCABLE_BIN override: an engine binary reached with no IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR
# cannot find reference/*.md (so native platform refs never inline) or read its
# own version (so UPDATE_AVAILABLE never fires). Setting it here covers every
# candidate the launcher can exec.
: "${IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR:=$skill_dir}"
: "${IMPECCABLE_SELF:=$0}"
export IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR IMPECCABLE_SELF

if [ -n "${IMPECCABLE_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "${IMPECCABLE_BIN}" ]; then
  exec "${IMPECCABLE_BIN}" "$@"
fi

# Windows names itself in the environment, which saves a process there; one
# uname covers the rest. PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE is what impeccable.cmd reads,
# so both launchers pick the same cached engine (AMD64 under x64 Git Bash on
# ARM64, as uname -m reported before).
if [ "${OS:-}" = Windows_NT ]; then
  sys="Windows_NT ${PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE:-unknown}"
else
  sys=$(uname -sm 2>/dev/null) || sys="unknown unknown"
fi
case "${sys%% *}" in
  Darwin) os=darwin ;;
  Linux) os=linux ;;
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) os=windows ;;
  *) os=unknown ;;
esac
case "${sys##* }" in
  arm64|aarch64|ARM64) arch=arm64 ;;
  x86_64|amd64|AMD64) arch=x64 ;;
  *) arch=unknown ;;
esac

version=""
[ -f "$dir/VERSION" ] && { IFS="$ws" read -r version _ < "$dir/VERSION" || :; }
bin="$dir/bin/$os-$arch/impeccable"
[ "$os" = windows ] && bin="$bin.exe"

# Lost the executable bit in transit (zip extraction, some copiers).
if [ -f "$bin" ] && { [ -x "$bin" ] || chmod +x "$bin" 2>/dev/null; }; then
  if [ -n "$probing" ] || [ -z "$version" ] || { probe_ok "$bin" && [ "$probe_version" = "$version" ]; }; then
    exec "$bin" "$@"
  fi
  echo "impeccable: skipping $bin: it reports engine ${probe_version:-unknown} but this skill pins $version; delete it to stop this warning" >&2
fi
# On Windows (an MSYS/Git Bash shell) the cached names carry .exe so this
# launcher and impeccable.cmd share one cache.
exe=""
[ "$os" = windows ] && exe=".exe"
home_bin="${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.impeccable/bin/impeccable$exe"
if [ -z "$probing" ] && [ -x "$home_bin" ] && probe_ok "$home_bin"; then
  exec "$home_bin" "$@"
fi
# Version-pinned user cache, filled by the download below or by `impeccable update`.
cache_root="${IMPECCABLE_HOME:-${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.impeccable}"
cached="$cache_root/bin/$version/impeccable$exe"
asset="impeccable-$os-$arch"
[ "$os" = windows ] && asset="$asset.exe"
if [ -n "$version" ] && [ -x "$cached" ]; then
  read_expected
  cached_size
  stamp=""
  stamp_size=""
  { IFS="$ws" read -r stamp stamp_size _ < "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :
  if [ -n "$stamp" ] && [ "$stamp_size" = "$size" ] && { [ "$stamp" = "$expected" ] || [ "$stamp" = "$expected_x64" ]; } && [ ! "$cached" -nt "$cached.verified" ]; then
    exec "$cached" "$@"
  fi
  hash_file "$cached"
  if [ -n "$actual" ] && { [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || [ "$actual" = "$expected_x64" ]; }; then
    { echo "$actual $size" > "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :
    exec "$cached" "$@"
  fi
  echo "impeccable: cannot verify the cached engine $cached against $manifest; not using it" >&2
fi
if [ -z "$probing" ] && command -v impeccable >/dev/null 2>&1 && probe_ok impeccable; then
  exec impeccable "$@"
fi

# Last resort: fetch this version's binary for the current platform from the
# public release channel into the user cache. Needs network; sandboxes without
# egress preinstall the binary on PATH instead.
setup_help() {
  echo "Engine $version setup needs network access and write permission to $cache_root/bin/$version." >&2
  echo "Run this launcher ($0) with engine-probe in a terminal that has those permissions, then retry the original command." >&2
  echo "Alternatively, set IMPECCABLE_HOME to a writable cache location, or IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary." >&2
}
fetch_url() {
  http_status=""
  download_host=""
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fetch_result=0
    metadata=$(curl -fsSL --retry 2 -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}' -o "$tmp" "$1" 2>/dev/null) || fetch_result=$?
    http_status=${metadata%% *}
    effective_url=${metadata#* }
    # Only the authority is needed, never the signed storage URL's query.
    download_host=${effective_url#*://}
    download_host=${download_host%%/*}
    download_host=${download_host##*@}
    case "$download_host" in
      \[*) download_host=${download_host%%]*}] ;;
      *) download_host=${download_host%%:*} ;;
    esac
    download_host=$(printf '%s' "$download_host" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    return "$fetch_result"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -q -O "$tmp" "$1" 2>/dev/null
  else
    return 1
  fi
}
check_download() {
  download_file=${1:-$tmp}
  if [ ! -f "$download_file" ]; then
    echo "impeccable: download completed but the file was removed before execution: $url; check your antivirus quarantine or logs. Refusing to continue; do not disable protection." >&2
    exit 127
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$download_file" ]; then
    rm -f "$download_file"
    echo "impeccable: downloaded file is empty: $url; refusing the unverified download" >&2
    exit 127
  fi
}
if [ -n "$probing" ]; then
  # Inside another launcher's probe: no download, fail fast and quiet.
  exit 127
fi
if [ -n "$version" ] && [ "$os" != unknown ] && [ "$arch" != unknown ]; then
  base="${IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE:-https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases/download}"
  url="$base/engine-v$version/$asset"
  read_expected
  # Fail closed before any network traffic or cache write.
  if [ -z "$expected" ] && [ -z "$expected_x64" ]; then
    echo "impeccable: no checksum for engine $version ($asset) in $manifest; refusing the unverified download" >&2
    exit 127
  fi
  tmp="$cache_root/bin/$version/.impeccable.part.$$"
  # An interrupted download (Ctrl-C, a hook timeout) would otherwise leave the
  # PID-named staging file behind for good. The handlers must exit explicitly.
  cleanup() { rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || :; }
  trap 'cleanup; exit 129' HUP
  trap 'cleanup; exit 130' INT
  trap 'cleanup; exit 143' TERM
  if ! mkdir -p "$cache_root/bin/$version" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "impeccable: engine $version is not installed; cannot create cache directory: $cache_root/bin/$version" >&2
    setup_help
    exit 127
  fi
  # Check the actual staging file, not just directory existence: a cache from
  # an earlier run can be readable but no longer writable inside a sandbox.
  if ! (umask 077; : > "$tmp") 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "impeccable: engine $version is not installed; cannot write to cache directory: $cache_root/bin/$version" >&2
    setup_help
    exit 127
  fi
  fetched=0
  if [ -n "$expected" ] && fetch_url "$url"; then
    fetched=1
  elif [ -n "$expected_x64" ]; then
    # Windows on ARM runs x64 binaries; fall back when no arm64 asset exists.
    url="$base/engine-v$version/impeccable-windows-x64.exe"
    expected=$expected_x64
    fetch_url "$url" && fetched=1
  fi
  if [ "$fetched" = 1 ]; then
    check_download
    # No sha256 tool refuses the download too.
    hash_file "$tmp"
    check_download
    if [ -z "$actual" ]; then
      rm -f "$tmp"
      echo "impeccable: cannot verify $url (no sha256 tool, or hashing failed); refusing the unverified download" >&2
      exit 127
    fi
    if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
      rm -f "$tmp"
      echo "impeccable: checksum mismatch downloading $url" >&2
      exit 127
    fi
    check_download
    if ! chmod +x "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
      check_download
      rm -f "$tmp"
      echo "impeccable: could not make the verified download executable: $url" >&2
      exit 127
    fi
    check_download
    if ! mv -f "$tmp" "$cached" 2>/dev/null; then
      check_download
      rm -f "$tmp"
      echo "impeccable: could not cache the verified download: $url" >&2
      exit 127
    fi
    check_download "$cached"
    cached_size
    { echo "$actual $size" > "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :
    exec "$cached" "$@"
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  case "$http_status" in
    5[0-9][0-9])
      case "$download_host" in
        github.com|*.github.com|githubusercontent.com|*.githubusercontent.com)
          echo "impeccable: could not download engine $version: GitHub's downloads are failing right now (HTTP $http_status from $download_host). This is an outage on GitHub's side, not a problem with your setup or the CLI, so updating won't help. Check https://www.githubstatus.com and run the same command again once GitHub has recovered." >&2 ;;
        *)
          echo "impeccable: could not download engine $version: $download_host is failing right now (HTTP $http_status), a server error on $download_host's side. Try again later." >&2 ;;
      esac
      exit 127 ;;
  esac
  echo "impeccable: could not download engine $version from $url; check network access, the release URL, and curl or wget availability." >&2
  setup_help
  exit 127
fi

echo "impeccable: no engine binary for $os-$arch found (looked in $bin, $cached, PATH)." >&2
echo "Download impeccable-$os-$arch from https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases (tag engine-v$version) into $cache_root/bin/$version/impeccable$exe (then chmod +x), or set IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. Docs: https://impeccable.style" >&2
exit 127

@echo off
setlocal
rem Impeccable launcher (Windows). Runs bin\windows-<arch>\impeccable.exe next
rem to this file, else a cached or freshly downloaded engine binary.
rem
rem Structure notes (this file is exercised by dry parsing and string-level
rem tests, not yet on a real Windows machine):
rem - No multi-line parenthesized blocks: cmd expands %var% at block parse
rem   time, which made the old download path read back empty %url%/%cached%.
rem   Linear goto flow keeps every expansion on its own line, and avoids
rem   delayed expansion eating ! characters in user arguments.
rem - The unversioned user binary and the PATH candidate are validated with
rem   the engine-probe handshake (see :probe) so the retired 3.x npm CLI,
rem   whose bin is also named impeccable, is never exec'd. The sibling binary
rem   must also report the version in VERSION: it is not tracked, so a skill
rem   upgrade can leave an old engine in place. IMPECCABLE_BIN stays trusted.
rem - Downloads and the version-pinned cache are verified via certutil
rem   against engine-checksums.txt next to this file, and fail closed; a
rem   .verified stamp lets later runs skip hashing the cache while it holds
rem   the manifest digest and the binary's size and is not older than the
rem   binary. On ARM64 the arm64 asset is tried first and the x64 asset is the
rem   fallback (Windows on ARM runs x64 binaries), each only when the manifest
rem   has a line for it.
if not defined IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR set "IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR=%~dp0.."
if not defined IMPECCABLE_SELF set "IMPECCABLE_SELF=%~f0"
set "arch=x64"
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set "arch=arm64"

if not defined IMPECCABLE_BIN goto no_env_bin
if not exist "%IMPECCABLE_BIN%" goto no_env_bin
set "run=%IMPECCABLE_BIN%"
goto run
:no_env_bin

set "version="
if exist "%~dp0VERSION" set /p version=<"%~dp0VERSION"
set "bin=%~dp0bin\windows-%arch%\impeccable.exe"
if not exist "%bin%" goto no_sibling
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto sibling_ok
if not defined version goto sibling_ok
call :probe "%bin%"
if "%probe_version%"=="%version%" goto sibling_ok
if not defined probe_version set "probe_version=unknown"
echo impeccable: skipping "%bin%": it reports engine %probe_version% but this skill pins %version%; delete it to stop this warning 1>&2
goto no_sibling
:sibling_ok
set "run=%bin%"
goto run
:no_sibling

set "home_bin=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable\bin\impeccable.exe"
if not exist "%home_bin%" goto no_home_bin
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto no_home_bin
call :probe "%home_bin%"
if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto no_home_bin
set "run=%home_bin%"
goto run
:no_home_bin

if not defined IMPECCABLE_HOME set "IMPECCABLE_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable"
set "cached=%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\impeccable.exe"
set "asset=impeccable-windows-%arch%.exe"
set "manifest=%~dp0engine-checksums.txt"
if not defined version goto no_cache
if not exist "%cached%" goto no_cache
call :read_expected
for %%f in ("%cached%") do set "size=%%~zf"
set "stamp="
if exist "%cached%.verified" for /f "usebackq tokens=1,2" %%s in ("%cached%.verified") do set "stamp=%%s"& set "stamp_size=%%t"
if not defined stamp goto cache_hash
if not "%stamp_size%"=="%size%" goto cache_hash
if /I "%stamp%"=="%expected%" goto cache_stamp_matches
if /I "%stamp%"=="%expected_x64%" goto cache_stamp_matches
goto cache_hash
:cache_stamp_matches
rem Newest first: the stamp must be listed before the binary it vouches for.
set "newest="
for /f "delims=" %%f in ('dir /b /a:-d /o:-d "%cached%*" 2^>nul') do if not defined newest set "newest=%%f"
if /I "%newest%"=="impeccable.exe.verified" goto cache_trusted
:cache_hash
call :sha256 "%cached%" "%TEMP%\impeccable-hash-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%.txt"
if not defined actual goto cache_unverified
if /I "%actual%"=="%expected%" goto cache_verified
if /I "%actual%"=="%expected_x64%" goto cache_verified
:cache_unverified
echo impeccable: cannot verify the cached engine "%cached%" against "%manifest%"; not using it 1>&2
goto no_cache
:cache_verified
(>"%cached%.verified" echo %actual% %size%) 2>nul
:cache_trusted
set "run=%cached%"
goto run
:no_cache

if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto download
rem The first impeccable on PATH, resolved once so the probe and the run see
rem the same file. A batch shim (npm writes impeccable.cmd) must run under
rem call to return here (#1240), and call expands % in the arguments a second
rem time; a real binary runs directly so a target such as a%20b reaches it intact.
set "path_bin="
rem where also lists npm's extensionless POSIX shim, which cmd cannot run:
rem take the first match with a runnable extension.
rem Loop letters c and k are not path modifiers, so %%~xc reads as the
rem extension of c and never as a loop variable followed by text.
for /f "delims=" %%c in ('where impeccable 2^>nul') do if not defined path_bin for %%k in (.exe .com .cmd .bat) do if /I "%%~xc"=="%%k" set "path_bin=%%c"
if not defined path_bin goto download
call :probe "%path_bin%"
if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto download
for %%k in ("%path_bin%") do set "path_ext=%%~xk"
if /I "%path_ext%"==".cmd" goto path_shim
if /I "%path_ext%"==".bat" goto path_shim
"%path_bin%" %*
exit /b %errorlevel%
:path_shim
call "%path_bin%" %*
exit /b %errorlevel%

:download
rem Last resort: fetch this version's binary from the release channel into
rem the version-pinned user cache, verify it, then run it. Never inside
rem another launcher's probe: fail fast and quiet instead.
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE exit /b 127
if not defined version goto fail
call :read_expected
if not defined expected if not defined expected_x64 goto no_checksum
where curl.exe >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto curl_missing
if not defined IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE set "IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE=https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases/download"
if exist "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\" goto cache_ready
mkdir "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto cache_directory_failed
:cache_ready
rem Stage the download in a directory only this run owns, as the sh launcher
rem does with .impeccable.part.$$: concurrent first runs (parallel hooks, two
rem agents) must never write, hash or move each other's files. mkdir fails
rem when the name exists, so it claims the name atomically. RANDOM alone is
rem not enough because cmd seeds it from the clock in whole seconds; the
rem timestamp and the retry on collision keep same-second runs apart. A cache
rem directory that refuses every mkdir is reported as unwritable.
set "attempt=0"
:claim_staging
set /a attempt+=1
if %attempt% GTR 20 goto cache_write_failed
set "stamp=%TIME: =0%"
set "stamp=%stamp::=%"
set "stamp=%stamp:.=%"
set "stamp=%stamp:,=%"
set "staging=%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\.impeccable.part.%stamp%-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%"
mkdir "%staging%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto claim_staging
set "part=%staging%\impeccable.exe"
rem Redirection failures do not reliably update ERRORLEVEL in cmd.exe;
rem branch on the command's failure directly.
(type nul >"%part%") 2>nul || goto staging_write_failed
set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
if not defined expected goto fetch_x64
call :fetch_url
if not errorlevel 1 goto verify
:fetch_x64
if not defined expected_x64 goto download_failed
set "asset=impeccable-windows-x64.exe"
set "expected=%expected_x64%"
set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
call :fetch_url
if errorlevel 1 goto download_failed

:verify
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
rem Mirrors the sh launcher and fails closed: a freshly downloaded binary
rem runs only after its hash matches the digest read from engine-checksums.txt.
rem An empty certutil result refuses the download instead of running an
rem unverified binary.
call :sha256 "%part%" "%staging%\hash.txt"
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
if not defined actual goto verify_refuse
if /I "%actual%"=="%expected%" goto place
call :discard_staging
echo impeccable: checksum mismatch downloading %url% 1>&2
exit /b 127

:verify_refuse
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
call :discard_staging
echo impeccable: cannot verify %url% (certutil could not hash it); refusing the unverified download 1>&2
exit /b 127

:fetch_url
set "http_status="
set "effective_url="
set "download_host="
curl.exe -fsSL --retry 2 -w "%%{http_code} %%{url_effective}" -o "%part%" "%url%" >"%staging%\http.txt" 2>nul
set "fetch_result=%errorlevel%"
for /f "usebackq tokens=1" %%a in ("%staging%\http.txt") do set "http_status=%%a"
for /f "usebackq tokens=2" %%a in ("%staging%\http.txt") do set "effective_url=%%a"
rem Token 2 is the authority after scheme://. Drop userinfo and the port.
for /f "tokens=2 delims=/" %%h in ("%effective_url%") do set "download_host=%%h"
for /f "tokens=1,* delims=@" %%h in ("%download_host%") do if not "%%i"=="" set "download_host=%%i"
rem Bracketed IPv6 hosts contain colons that are not port separators.
if "%download_host:~0,1%"=="[" goto fetch_ipv6
for /f "tokens=1 delims=:" %%h in ("%download_host%") do set "download_host=%%h"
exit /b %fetch_result%
:fetch_ipv6
for /f "tokens=1 delims=]" %%h in ("%download_host%") do set "download_host=%%h]"
exit /b %fetch_result%

:read_expected
rem Sets expected (and, on ARM64, expected_x64: Windows on ARM runs x64
rem binaries) from engine-checksums.txt.
call :manifest_digest "%asset%" expected
set "expected_x64="
if "%arch%"=="arm64" call :manifest_digest impeccable-windows-x64.exe expected_x64
exit /b 0

:manifest_digest
rem Sets the variable named %2 to the digest the first engine-checksums.txt
rem line for this version and asset %1 records, empty when there is none.
set "%~2="
if not exist "%manifest%" exit /b 0
for /f "usebackq tokens=1-3" %%a in ("%manifest%") do if "%%a"=="%version%" if /I "%%b"=="%~1" if not defined %~2 set "%~2=%%c"
exit /b 0

:sha256
rem Sets actual to the sha256 of %~1, empty when certutil fails. %~2 is the
rem scratch file for its output. Check certutil's status before parsing: its
rem error text on stdout is not a digest.
set "actual="
certutil -hashfile "%~1" SHA256 >"%~2" 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto sha256_done
for /f "usebackq skip=1 delims=" %%h in ("%~2") do if not defined actual set "actual=%%h"
if not defined actual goto sha256_done
set "actual=%actual: =%"
:sha256_done
del "%~2" >nul 2>nul
exit /b 0

:check_download
set "download_file=%~1"
if not defined download_file set "download_file=%part%"
if not exist "%download_file%" goto download_missing
for %%f in ("%download_file%") do if %%~zf==0 goto download_empty
exit /b 0

:download_missing
call :discard_staging
echo impeccable: download completed but the file was removed before execution: %url%; check your antivirus quarantine or logs. Refusing to continue; do not disable protection. 1>&2
exit /b 127

:download_empty
del "%download_file%" >nul 2>nul
call :discard_staging
echo impeccable: downloaded file is empty: %url%; refusing the unverified download 1>&2
exit /b 127

:discard_staging
rem Removes this run's staging directory and whatever is left in it. Never
rem touches another run's staging directory or the cached binary.
if defined staging rd /s /q "%staging%" >nul 2>nul
exit /b 0

:place
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
move /y "%part%" "%cached%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto place_failed
call :discard_staging
call :check_download "%cached%"
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
for %%f in ("%cached%") do set "size=%%~zf"
(>"%cached%.verified" echo %actual% %size%) 2>nul
set "run=%cached%"
goto run

:place_failed
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
call :discard_staging
echo impeccable: could not cache the verified download: %url% 1>&2
exit /b 127

:run
"%run%" %*
exit /b %errorlevel%

:probe
rem Sets probe_ok=1 when %1 answers the engine handshake: prints
rem "impeccable-engine <version>" and exits 0, and probe_version to that
rem version. The 3.x npm CLI answers any unknown verb with "Unknown command",
rem exit 1, so it never passes.
rem The candidate runs under call: an npm .cmd shim run without it takes
rem over this script and never returns (#1240).
set "probe_ok="
set "probe_version="
set "probe_tmp=%TEMP%\impeccable-probe-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%.txt"
set "IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE=1"
call "%~1" engine-probe >"%probe_tmp%" 2>nul
set "probe_err=%ERRORLEVEL%"
set "IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE="
if not "%probe_err%"=="0" goto probe_done
findstr /b /c:"impeccable-engine" "%probe_tmp%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto probe_done
set "probe_ok=1"
for /f "usebackq tokens=2" %%v in ("%probe_tmp%") do if not defined probe_version set "probe_version=%%v"
:probe_done
del "%probe_tmp%" >nul 2>nul
exit /b 0

:no_checksum
echo impeccable: no checksum for engine %version% (%asset%) in "%manifest%"; refusing the unverified download 1>&2
exit /b 127

:cache_directory_failed
echo impeccable: engine %version% is not installed; cannot create cache directory: "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" 1>&2
goto setup_failed

:staging_write_failed
call :discard_staging

:cache_write_failed
echo impeccable: engine %version% is not installed; cannot write to cache directory: "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" 1>&2
goto setup_failed

:curl_missing
echo impeccable: cannot download engine %version%; curl.exe is unavailable. 1>&2
goto setup_failed

:download_failed
call :discard_staging
if not "%http_status:~0,1%"=="5" goto download_generic
if "%http_status:~2,1%"=="" goto download_generic
if /I "%download_host%"=="github.com" goto download_github
if /I "%download_host:~-11%"==".github.com" goto download_github
if /I "%download_host%"=="githubusercontent.com" goto download_github
if /I "%download_host:~-22%"==".githubusercontent.com" goto download_github
echo impeccable: could not download engine %version%: %download_host% is failing right now (HTTP %http_status%), a server error on %download_host%'s side. Try again later. 1>&2
exit /b 127
:download_github
echo impeccable: could not download engine %version%: GitHub's downloads are failing right now (HTTP %http_status% from %download_host%). This is an outage on GitHub's side, not a problem with your setup or the CLI, so updating won't help. Check https://www.githubstatus.com and run the same command again once GitHub has recovered. 1>&2
exit /b 127
:download_generic
echo impeccable: could not download engine %version% from %url%; check network access and the release URL. 1>&2

:setup_failed
echo Engine %version% setup needs network access and write permission to "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%". 1>&2
echo Run this launcher ("%~f0") with engine-probe in a terminal that has those permissions, then retry the original command. 1>&2
echo Alternatively, set IMPECCABLE_HOME to a writable cache location, or IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. 1>&2
exit /b 127

:fail
echo impeccable: no engine binary found (looked in %bin%, %cached%, PATH). 1>&2
echo Download impeccable-windows-%arch%.exe from https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases (tag engine-v%version%) and save it as %cached%, or set IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. Docs: https://impeccable.style 1>&2
exit /b 127

The `skill/reference/ios.md` and `skill/reference/android.md` platform reference files are distilled from ehmo's `platform-design-skills` (Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Material Design 3 rules), rewritten in Impeccable's voice.

**Original work:** https://github.com/ehmo/platform-design-skills

**Albert Sans** (`albertsans.ttf`)
**Original work:** https://github.com/usted/Albert-Sans
**Original license:** SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`albertsans-OFL.txt`)
**Copyright:** 2021 The Albert Sans Project Authors

**Original work:** https://github.com/googlefonts/alumni
**Original license:** SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`alumnisans-OFL.txt`)

## Consent rules in the browser extension

The browser extension's journeys answer cookie and consent banners with DuckDuckGo's autoconsent: its engine and rule set, unmodified, ship in `extension/walks/consent-rules.js` behind a small bridge of our own.

**Original work:** https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent (its `dist/autoconsent.playwright.js` and `rules/compact-rules.json`, at the version named on the first line of `consent-rules.js`)

files.README.md:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --sarif src/ # SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description npx impeccable detect --report-unused-ignores src/ # inline ignores that waive nothing ``` GitHub code scanning keeps these alerts on the pull request, lets reviewers dismiss them, and fails only on findings that are new in that PR. `--github` annotates a single Actions run; `--sarif` is the log you upload: ```yaml permissions: contents: read security-events: write steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: npx impeccable detect --sarif src/ > impeccable.sarif || test $? -eq 2 - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3 with: sarif_file: impeccable.sarif category: impeccable ``` Exit code `2` (findings) still uploads the log; exit code `1` (a target couldn't be scanned) fails the step, and the log it wrote says `executionSuccessful: false` so it is never read as a clean scan. `category` keeps this upload beside CodeQL instead of replacing it. Run it from the repository root: paths are written relative to `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, and a file outside it becomes a `file://` URI. A clean scan still prints a log with an empty `results` array, which is what closes alerts that were fixed. HTML findings without a line are anchored to the file. The upload action fills `partialFingerprints.primaryLocationLineHash`; detect leaves it unset. Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. An HTML file scan reads the pixels of a local background image that is the ground behind text, so white copy on a near-white photo fails a CI gate without a browser. An image that only decorates its box is left alone, and a remote image is never fetched. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. When that comment no longer matches a finding it will swallow the next one; `npx impeccable detect --report-unused-ignores src/` names each stale waiver so CI fails on it instead. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/ignore.md`. Critique reports stay local unless `reports.commit` is true. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.
Copy the .gitignore entries ```gitignore # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/ignore.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end ```
The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached `. ## Good to know **Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **Native apps.** Set `## Platform` in `PRODUCT.md` to `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive` (one Flutter or React Native codebase that follows each OS), and the design commands work from Apple's HIG or Material 3 instead of web conventions. `init` asks when it can't tell. `audit` and `adapt` switch to native versions, and the native audit reads SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, or Flutter source directly. The detector, live mode with its `generate` shortcut, and the edit hook stay web-only, because they work on HTML and CSS in a browser. **Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. **Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor). **Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy). ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues) for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see [DEVELOP.md](docs/DEVELOP.md). - [Changelog](https://impeccable.style/changelog) for what shipped. - Follow [@pbakaus](https://x.com/pbakaus) for release notes and new rules. ## Sponsors [![CI powered by Namespace](https://namespace.so/oss/badge.svg)](https://namespace.so/github-actions/?utm_source=oss&utm_campaign=impeccable) Thanks to [Namespace](https://namespace.so) for sponsoring Impeccable's CI with fast Linux and Windows runners. ## License Apache 2.0. files.HOW-TO-USE.md:
# Design with Intent

Intent is a UX design strategy system made of six specialized agents. Each is a self-contained system prompt you paste into a Claude Project (or similar). Together they cover the full arc of design work — from framing the problem to packaging the design for the build.

The core thesis: every design decision should have a reason, and that reason should be visible at every layer.

---

## The agents

| Agent | File | Use when... |
|-------|------|-------------|
| **Noor** (Entry Point) | `noor.md` | Starting a project, setting context, routing to specialists, presenting the work |
| **Ember** (Strategy + Research) | `ember.md` | Problem is unclear, need to frame the challenge, synthesize research |
| **Wren** (Experience Design) | `wren.md` | Designing flows, organizing information, wireframing screens, writing interface copy, mapping the service behind it |
| **Vigil** (Quality + Resilience) | `vigil.md` | Evaluating quality, hardening for edge cases, ensuring accessibility, measuring whether it worked |
| **Rune** (Handoff) | `rune.md` | The design is approved and someone needs to build it |
| **Sage** (Philosopher) | `sage.md` | Stuck, need to brainstorm, problem feels underexplored |

---

## How to deploy

### Option 1: Claude Projects (recommended)

1. Create a new Claude Project
2. Copy the contents of the relevant agent file into the Project's custom instructions
3. Add your project context — briefs, research, system documentation, constraints
4. Start working. Claude will operate as that specialized agent.

**Tip:** For most projects, start with Noor. She will help you establish context and point you to the right specialist.

### Option 2: Direct prompting

Paste the agent instructions at the start of a conversation:

```
[Paste contents of noor.md]

---

Now, here's my project: [describe your project]
```

This works for quick sessions where you do not need a full Project setup.

### Option 3: Chained workflow

For complex projects, use agents in sequence. Each agent's output becomes the next agent's input.

1. **Noor** — Establish project context (users, product, constraints, ethical stance)
2. **Ember** — Frame the problem, synthesize research, define scope
3. **Wren** — Design flows, structure information, write the interface copy
4. **Vigil** — Evaluate the design, harden for edge cases, check accessibility
5. **Rune** — Check readiness, run the ethical review, and package the artifacts for the build

Start a new Project (or conversation) for each agent. Carry the prior agent's output forward as context.

**Sage** is not a sequential step. She is available at any point when the team needs to step back and think before moving forward.

### Option 4: Claude Code plugin

If you use Claude Code, install the Intent plugin; all 6 agents and 18 skills register automatically:

```
/plugin marketplace add ghaida/intent
/plugin install intent@intent
```

Then in any Claude Code session:

- **Invoke agents** as subagents via `@<name>` — e.g., `@ember help me frame this problem`, `@vigil audit this flow`, `@wren design the signup`.
- **Invoke skills** as slash commands — `/intent:strategize`, `/intent:journey`, `/intent:evaluate`, etc.

**Tip:** This is the fastest path for Claude Code users. No per-project copy-paste. All 6 agents and 18 skills are one plugin install away.

---

## Quick decision tree

```
START: I have a design challenge

├── "I don't know what problem we're solving"
│   └── Ember
│      Frames problems, synthesizes research, defines scope
│
├── "I need to design the experience"
│   └── Wren
│      Flows, navigation, information architecture, interface copy
│
├── "Is this actually good? Does it work for everyone?"
│   └── Vigil
│      Evaluates quality, hardens for real conditions, ensures access
│
├── "Ready to build"
│   └── Rune
│      Readiness, the ethical review, the handoff package
│
├── "I'm stuck / brainstorm / what am I missing?"
│   └── Sage
│      Sits with problems, expands thinking, challenges assumptions
│
└── "I need to set up the project context"
    └── Noor
       Orients, gathers context, holds principles, routes to specialists
```

**Note:** Sage is a cross-cutting cognitive mode, not a sequential phase. Any agent can benefit from Sage's expansive thinking when the problem needs more exploration before the next move. You can also use Sage standalone for pure brainstorming.

---

## Project lifecycle examples

### Small project (2-4 weeks)

**Noor --> Ember --> Wren --> Rune**

- Noor: Establish context — users, constraints, ethical stance
- Ember: Quick 2-page brief with problem framing and scope
- Wren: Design the flow, write the copy
- Rune: Package the design for the build
- Sage: Available at any point if the team gets stuck or the framing feels shallow

### Medium project (6-12 weeks)

**Noor --> Ember --> Wren --> Vigil --> Rune**

- Noor: Full context gathering, including competitive landscape
- Ember: Complete brief with research synthesis, hypothesis, five foundational questions
- Wren: User flows across devices, information architecture, content strategy
- Vigil: Heuristic evaluation, accessibility audit, edge case hardening
- Rune: The handoff package, with the ethical review logged
- Sage: Enter from any agent when exploration is needed — when the brief feels too tidy or the direction is not clicking

### Large project (12-26 weeks)

**All agents with iteration loops**

- Noor: Context document that becomes the project's source of truth
- Ember: Brief, hypothesis, market analysis, five foundational questions
- Wren: Flows across all devices and audience contexts, full IA, content strategy
- Vigil: Quality evaluation, resilience testing, accessibility audit, anti-pattern scan
- Rune: The handoff package, readiness checked and the ethical review logged
- Sage: Use at project kickoff, at phase transitions, or whenever the team senses the problem is being solved too quickly
- Loop back to Ember if testing reveals new insights

---

## What each agent produces

### Noor (Entry Point)
- Project context documents
- Anti-pattern flags with severity and regulatory notes
- Routing recommendations to specialists
- Principle-grounded framing of design decisions

### Ember (Strategy + Research)
- Design briefs (3-5 pages)
- Research synthesis documents (5-10 pages)
- Opportunity assessments with quantified impact
- Hypothesis statements for A/B tests
- Five foundational questions assessments
- Project scoping documents (will do / will not do)

### Wren (Experience Design)
- Screen-by-screen user flows
- Device-specific variants (mobile, web, TV)
- Information architecture and navigation structures
- Content strategy and voice guidelines
- Copy specifications and microcopy
- Interaction specs with state documentation
- Service blueprints: frontstage, backstage, support, dependencies, failure modes

### Vigil (Quality + Resilience)
- Severity-ranked findings with a verdict per heuristic
- Anti-pattern verdicts with regulatory context
- Cognitive walkthrough results (per-task, per-step)
- Edge case and error recovery documentation
- Accessibility audits against WCAG
- Prioritized remediation roadmaps
- Measurement frameworks: Goal-Signal-Metric chains, A/B test plans, learning plans

### Rune (Handoff)
- A readiness check: the brief and the full-page wireframes approved, every journey screen drawn
- The ethical review, logged as a decision
- The handoff package: the project's artifacts with one entry page that says what the product is, what is in the package, how the pieces fit, and what is left to the builder

### Sage (Philosopher)
- Reframed problem statements
- Surfaced assumptions the team did not know it was making
- Cross-domain connections and structural analogies
- Open questions that change the direction of inquiry
- Synthesized insights translated back into the active agent's language

---

## Shared principles

Every agent in the Intent system follows these:

1. **Evidence-grounded.** Every decision cites evidence or is logged as a judgment call.
2. **Problem-first.** Frame the problem before proposing solutions.
3. **Gaps in the record.** What is not known is an open question in the work or a note in the log, never a sentence of hedging.
4. **Ecosystem thinking.** Design for the full context — not just the screen in front of the user.
5. **Log the "no".** What was chosen against, and why, is in the decision log.

And the six core UX principles that Noor holds:

- Respect user autonomy
- Design for real conditions
- Make intent visible
- Evidence over intuition
- Systems over screens
- Ethical defaults

---

## Tips for best results

### Be specific about context

Instead of: "Design a signup flow"

Try: "Design a signup flow for users arriving from a partner referral on mobile. They may not know they have access. The goal is 80% activation within 7 days."

Context changes everything. The more specific you are about users, constraints, and goals, the more useful the agent's output becomes.

### Provide existing materials

Upload relevant files to your Project:

- Prior research or briefs
- Existing system documentation
- Competitive examples
- Technical constraints documents
- Brand voice or design system guidelines

### Ask for the right output format

Each agent has a default output structure. You can also ask:

- "Give me a condensed 1-page version"
- "Expand the edge cases section"
- "Format this as a stakeholder presentation outline"
- "Just give me the priority issues, skip the full audit"

### Use agents to cross-review

- Have Vigil review Wren's flows for quality and accessibility
- Have Ember check Rune's package against the brief
- Have Vigil check Ember's brief for assumption gaps
- Have Sage question any agent's framing when it feels too tidy

---

## Files in this package

```
agents/noor.md   — Entry point. Context, principles, anti-patterns, routing.
agents/ember.md  — Strategy and research. Problem framing, briefs, synthesis.
agents/wren.md   — Experience design. Flows, IA, content, interaction.
agents/vigil.md  — Quality and resilience. Evaluation, hardening, accessibility.
agents/rune.md   — Handoff. Readiness, the ethical review, the package.
agents/sage.md   — Philosopher. Expansive thinking, assumption challenging.
HOW-TO-USE.md    — This file.
```

---

*Intent is a design reasoning system. It does not replace your judgment — it makes the reasoning behind your judgment visible, testable, and traceable. Design with intent.*

# Design with Intent

A comprehensive UX and design strategy system for AI tools. 18 specialized skills and 6 agents that cover the full product design practice, from early strategy and research through experience design, quality assurance, and engineering handoff.

Intent gives AI the context to approach design decisions with depth. Where visual design tools focus on how things look, Intent focuses on why they exist — research, strategy, systems thinking, flows, content, accessibility, ethics, and measurement.

## The agents

Six agents, each combining multiple skills into one specialist:

| Domain | Agent | Skills it combines |
|--------|-------|--------------------|
| Entry point + Presentation | **Noor** | `/intent` + `/present`: orients the project, holds UX principles and the anti-pattern catalog, routes to specialists, and presents the finished work |
| Strategy + Research | **Ember** | `/strategize` + `/investigate` + `/storytelling` — frames problems, demands evidence, gives the work its narrative shape |
| Experience Design | **Wren** | `/journey` + `/organize` + `/wireframe` + `/articulate` + `/blueprint` + `/transpose` + `/localize` — shapes user flows, structures information, wireframes screens, designs the words, maps the service behind them, and adapts the design across platforms and markets |
| Quality + Resilience | **Vigil** | `/evaluate` + `/fortify` + `/include` + `/measure` — evaluates UX quality, hardens for edge cases, ensures accessibility, measures whether it worked |
| Engineering Handoff | **Rune** | `/specify` — checks the design is ready, runs the ethical review, and packages the project's artifacts with one entry page that says how they fit |
| Cross-cutting Wisdom | **Sage** | `/philosopher` — sits with problems, expands thinking, challenges assumptions |

For larger projects, chain agents in sequence: Ember to frame the problem, Wren to design the experience, Vigil to ensure quality and accessibility, Rune to package it for the build. Sage can be entered at any point when the problem needs more exploration.

## The skills

17 discipline-specific skills plus the Intent foundation, organized by what you need done:

### Intent (foundation)

- `intent/SKILL.md` — Core UX principles, the anti-pattern catalog (72+ named deceptive, addictive, and manipulative patterns with severity ratings and regulatory context), context-gathering protocol, and skill routing logic.
- `intent/references/` — 8 deep reference documents covering research methods, information architecture, interaction patterns, content strategy, accessibility, service design, measurement frameworks, and ethical design.

### Strategy & Research

- `strategize/SKILL.md` — Problem framing through the Five Foundational Questions (problem validation, audience definition, solution fit, feature validation, competitive landscape). Research synthesis, opportunity sizing, hypothesis definition, competitive analysis.
- `investigate/SKILL.md` — Primary research execution and synthesis. Interview guide construction, usability test planning, survey design, diary studies, card sorts, tree tests. Synthesis frameworks: affinity mapping, thematic analysis, insight statements with counts and citations.
- `blueprint/SKILL.md` — Service blueprints, ecosystem maps, process architecture, dependency diagrams, system state and failure mode analysis, scalability planning. Offers visual companion output: rendered HTML diagrams, Pencil files, or structured specs for your design tool.

### Experience Design

- `journey/SKILL.md` — End-to-end user flow design. Task analysis, decision points, entry-to-outcome paths, device-aware design, context variation handling, multi-channel journey mapping. Offers visual companion output: rendered HTML flow diagrams, Pencil files, or structured specs for your design tool.
- `organize/SKILL.md` — Information architecture. Navigation patterns, taxonomy design, labeling systems, wayfinding, search and browse models, card sort and tree test methodology. Offers visual companion output: rendered HTML site maps and navigation mockups, Pencil files, or structured specs for your design tool.
- `wireframe/SKILL.md` — Structural screen design at wireframe fidelity. Thumbnail sketches, full-page grayscale wireframes, click-through prototypes, fidelity doctrine, and a three-layer wireframe language (container, content, annotation). Offers visual companion output: a self-contained HTML wireframe viewer with grid and slideshow modes, Figma frames, or pencil files.
- `articulate/SKILL.md` — UX writing and content strategy. Voice and tone frameworks, error message design, empty states, CTA hierarchy, microcopy patterns, content models, inclusive language.

### Quality & Evaluation

- `evaluate/SKILL.md` — Structured UX assessment. Heuristic evaluation (Nielsen's 10, severity-ranked findings), cognitive walkthroughs, anti-pattern detection, task success analysis. Routes findings to specific skills for resolution.
- `fortify/SKILL.md` — Edge cases and resilience. State inventory (9 states per screen), error recovery patterns, first-run experience design, stress testing, i18n readiness, timeout and latency handling.
- `include/SKILL.md` — Accessibility as a design discipline. WCAG 2.2 for designers, screen reader flow design, keyboard navigation, cognitive and motor accessibility, inclusive design beyond compliance, testing methodology.

### Adaptation & Context

- `transpose/SKILL.md` — Cross-platform UX adaptation. Context analysis, platform-specific conventions (iOS, Android, web, TV, kiosk, voice), content priority shifting, cross-device journey continuity.
- `localize/SKILL.md` — Cultural and linguistic adaptation. Cultural dimension analysis, RTL/LTR design, content expansion/contraction, visual and symbolic adaptation, market-specific compliance, localization testing.

### Measurement

- `measure/SKILL.md` — Success metrics and experimentation. HEART framework, Goal-Signal-Metric mapping, A/B test design, funnel analysis, qualitative-quantitative triangulation, ethical measurement.

### Cross-cutting

- `philosopher/SKILL.md` — Expansive brainstorming protocol. Three strict phases (problem immersion, associative expansion, synthesis only when invited). Intensity levels, structured check-ins, and integration with every other skill. A cognitive mode, not a phase.
- `storytelling/SKILL.md` — Narrative structure for design work. Four canonical patterns — protagonist-arc, choreography, situation/complication/resolution, what-is/what-could-be — each with a goal, shape, and named pathology. Restated inline in `journey`, `blueprint`, `strategize`, `evaluate`. Refuses to smooth user data into clean arcs, manufacture strategic tension, substitute emotional appeal for evidence, or engineer stakeholder assent by shortcut.

### Handoff

- `specify/SKILL.md`: packages an approved design for the build. The handoff is the project's own artifacts, with one entry page in front that says what the product is, what is in the package, how the pieces fit, and what is left to the builder. Checks readiness and runs the ethical review against the anti-pattern catalog first.
- `present/SKILL.md`: story-first decks for design work. Interviews for audience, feeling, action and sources; gets a story outline approved; builds in Google Slides (via .pptx), PowerPoint, Figma Slides or reveal.js. Carries a stance on what makes a good presentation and refuses invented evidence.

## Install

**All platforms (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and more):**
```
npx skills add ghaida/intent --all
```

**Claude Code plugin:**
```
/plugin marketplace add ghaida/intent
```
Then open `/plugin` in Claude Code to install. You'll get all 18 skills as slash commands and all 6 agents registered as subagents.

**Manual download:** Grab the latest zip from [releases](https://github.com/ghaida/intent/releases/latest).

## How to use

**In Claude Code:** After installing the plugin, skills are available as slash commands — `/intent:strategize`, `/intent:journey`, `/intent:evaluate`, etc. — and the 6 agents (Noor, Ember, Wren, Vigil, Rune, Sage) are invokable as subagents via `@<name>` (e.g., `@ember help me frame this problem`).

**Quick decision tree:**

```
I have a design challenge
│
├─ "I don't know what problem we're solving"
│  └─ /strategize
│
├─ "I need to design the experience"
│  └─ /journey + /organize + /wireframe + /articulate
│
├─ "Does this actually work? For everyone?"
│  └─ /evaluate + /fortify + /include
│
├─ "Ready to build"
│  └─ /specify
│
├─ "I'm stuck / brainstorm / sit with this"
│  └─ /philosopher
│
├─ "What's the story here? / This feels lifeless"
│  └─ /storytelling
│
└─ "I need to set up context for the project"
   └─ /intent
```

## The anti-pattern catalog

Intent includes a catalog of 72+ named UX anti-patterns across 9 categories — deceptive patterns, default manipulation, urgency fabrication, addictive design, attention exploitation, weaponized accessibility, vulnerable user exploitation, AI-specific dark patterns, and common UX failures. Each pattern is named, described, and rated by severity. The catalog includes regulatory context (GDPR, FTC, COPPA, California ARL, EU Digital Services Act).

The catalog lives in the Intent master skill and is referenced by `/evaluate` for detection and `/specify` for ethical review before handoff.

## License
